$comment: Presenter tour (DEV_GUIDE §9.4). Edit the text freely; `npm run tour:generate` keeps title, pillar, talkingPoints, expected, minutes and dmsRef, and refreshes runs from the fixture unless a step has "lockRuns": true.

steps.title: Retail vs “Your price”
talkingPoints: DMS today: dealers and retail customers see the same default price until a custom price display is built.
Shopware: one product, a Dealer customer-group rule with advanced prices. Retail sees one price; the dealer sees retail struck through and “Your price”.
No extension and no price-list app: it is standard Rule Builder + advanced pricing.
steps.expected: Retail: a single price. Dealer Admin: retail struck through, “Your price” at the dealer qty-1 price, and a tier table.

steps.title: Listing pages show the persona's price

runs.label: Open the category as Dealer Admin

talkingPoints: DMS 11/18 feedback: price-list customers saw the default price on the category page and only their price on the product page.
Shopware calculates prices in the customer's context for listings too (calculatedPrice / cheapest price), so the card already shows “Your price”.
Same Store API call for every persona; the context token decides the price.
steps.expected: Every card shows the dealer qty-1 price labelled “Your price”, not the retail price.

steps.title: Quantity tiers on the PDP and in the cart

runs.label: Open the cart with 4 in it

talkingPoints: DMS needed quantity-break pricing visible on the product page and honoured in the cart.
Shopware advanced prices carry quantity ranges (1 / 5 / 10 / 25); the PDP tier table and the cart re-pricing both come from the same data.
Change the quantity from 4 to 5, then 10 and 25: the unit price steps down at each break with no custom code.
steps.expected: Cart line at qty 4 shows the next-break hint; changing to 5 / 10 / 25 lowers the unit price at each break.

steps.title: Cross-SKU series tiers (mix and match)

runs.label: Open the cart with 5 + 5 Velocity 70 Series

talkingPoints: DMS: quantities across SKUs in the same series must add up to reach a tier. BigCommerce needed a custom bridge app.
Shopware: an automatic promotion per series tier with a Rule Builder condition on the series quantity: 10+ saves 5%, 25+ saves 9.75%, the higher tier replaces the lower.
Front and rear shocks, any chassis, count together; other products in the cart do not. No code.
steps.expected: The cart shows a “Velocity 70 Series mix-and-match — 10+ tier” savings line. Set one line to 4 and it disappears.

steps.title: MAP: price hidden until the cart

runs.label: Open a MAP product as Retail

talkingPoints: DMS flags MAP items so the advertised price is not shown below MAP on listing and product pages.
The demo marks MAP items with a product custom field; the storefront shows “See price in cart” for retail and the real price in the cart.
This is a storefront rule (stated openly); dealers always see their price.
steps.expected: PDP and listings show “See price in cart” for Retail; the cart shows the real price.

steps.title: Shop by vehicle

runs.label: Shop Shocks for a 1982 Buick Regal

talkingPoints: DMS relies on a third-party search and fitment app on BigCommerce.
Here the year / make / model selector and My Garage filter category pages and search to parts that fit plus universal parts; the PDP shows a fit badge and a fitment table.
Fitment is a data file generated with the catalog, so a production build can swap in a full ACES/PIES fitment service without changing pages.
steps.expected: The fitment bar reads “Showing parts that fit 1982 Buick Regal”, the count drops, and each PDP shows Fits / Doesn't fit / Universal.

steps.title: Quick order pad

runs.label: Open quick order as the Junior Buyer

talkingPoints: DMS dealers order by part number in bulk; BigCommerce needed a quick-order add-on.
Type CPL-OL-X-8001 and KST-RB-X-7002 plus a made-up SKU, or paste rows from a spreadsheet: unknown SKUs get a row error, valid rows go to the cart or a list.
Built on Shopware's B2B Quick Order feature and the Store API product lookup.
steps.expected: The bad SKU row shows “Unknown SKU”; the valid rows are added and the mini-cart opens.

steps.title: Shopping lists
talkingPoints: DMS dealers reorder the same restock items every week from saved lists.
Shopware B2B Shopping Lists: shared by the company, add from any product page or the quick order pad, then add the whole list to the cart.
Click “Add all to cart”: 6 lines, priced for the dealer.
steps.expected: The list shows 6 items; “Add all to cart” fills the cart with 6 lines.

steps.title: Company, roles and permissions
talkingPoints: DMS needs company accounts where an owner manages buyers with limited rights.
Shopware B2B Employee Management: the Admin role has every permission; the Junior Buyer role can shop, use lists and quick order, and must request approval.
The Junior Buyer does not get the Company menu, and Shopware itself refuses the data (403), not just the UI.
steps.expected: Admin: employees with roles and a permission summary. Junior Buyer: no Company menu; the page explains the role cannot view it.

steps.title: Approval loop

runs.label: Junior Buyer: cart ready to submit

talkingPoints: DMS wants junior buyers to build carts that an owner approves before anything is ordered.
Shopware B2B Order Approval: an approval rule says every Junior Buyer cart needs the Admin role's approval. Submitting creates a pending request, not an order.
The Admin approves or declines with a comment; the Junior sees the result under My requests. In this demo no order is ever placed.
steps.expected: The cart shows the approval notice; after Submit, My requests shows Pending; the Admin approves it and the Junior sees Approved.
